Empirical Research Plan  
“Does financial development causally facilitate economic growth by relaxing external-finance constraints of industries?”

==================================================================
1. Identification Strategy
------------------------------------------------------------------
Method: Differences-in-Differences-in-Differences (DDD), i.e. an “interaction-in-panel” design.

•  First difference: high- vs. low-external-finance-dependence industries  
•  Second difference: countries with more vs. less developed domestic financial systems  
•  Third difference: time (initial year 1980 vs. end year 1990; annual panel possible)  

The coefficient on External-Dependenceᵢ × Financial-Development_ct × Post_t identifies whether industries that need more outside funding grow faster (in value added, capital formation, or number of firms) when they operate in countries with deeper financial systems after 1980.

Why appropriate?  
– Relies on plausibly exogenous cross-industry technological heterogeneity (measured from U.S. firms and therefore not mechanically related to conditions in other countries)  
– Exploits substantial cross-country variation in the depth of domestic finance at the starting point of the sample.  
– Difference-type design sweeps out all country-invariant industry factors, industry-invariant country factors, and global time shocks.

------------------------------------------------------------------
2. Treatment and Control
------------------------------------------------------------------
Treatment intensity variable:  
FINDEV_ct  = log(1 + Stock-market-cap/GDP)  or  log(1 + Private-credit/GDP)  
External-Finance-Dependenceᵢ  = (CapEx − CashFlow)/CapEx, computed from 1980s U.S. Compustat.

Key regressor: Treat_{ict} = Externalᵢ × FINDEV_ct × Post_t  

Where Post_t = 1 for years ≥ 1985 (mid-point) or simply compare growth 1980-1990.

Counterfactual / control:  
• Industries with low external dependence operating in the same country and year.  
• Same industry observed in countries with low financial development.  

No single event date → the “treatment” is continuous; the DDD term measures differential exposure.

------------------------------------------------------------------
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
------------------------------------------------------------------
A1. Parallel trends: Absent improvements in financial development, high- and low-external-dependence industries would have trended similarly within a country.  
Plausibility: External dependence is technological and measured from U.S. data; technology should evolve similarly across countries over one decade. We will test for pre-trends using 1970–1979 growth rates.

A2. Exogeneity of external-finance measure: The U.S.-based index is unrelated to industry-country shocks elsewhere.  
Plausibility: U.S.-only construction mitigates reflection of other countries’ conditions.

A3. Financial development is predetermined with respect to 1980–1990 industry-specific growth shocks.  
Plausibility: Legal origin, accounting standards, and historical factors drive FINDEV; use 1980 levels (or instrument with Legal-origin dummy) to strengthen.

A4. No simultaneous shocks differentially correlated with both FINDEV and high-external-dependence sectors.  
Addressed by rich controls and robustness checks (see §4).

------------------------------------------------------------------
4. Threats to Identification & Remedies
------------------------------------------------------------------
T1. Reverse causality: Booming high-tech/high-dependence sectors might themselves deepen local finance.  
Remedy: Use FINDEV measured in 1980 (predetermined), instrument FINDEV with legal-origin or CIFAR accounting-standards score, run 2SLS of FINDEV on IVs.

T2. Unobserved country-time shocks correlated with FINDEV (e.g., pro-market reforms) that may help all industries but especially capital-intensive ones.  
Remedy: Include country-year fixed effects interacted with capital-intensity; add controls for trade openness, macro stability; cluster SEs at country and industry levels (two-way clustering).

T3. Measurement error in industry value-added series across countries (especially developing economies).  
Remedy: Triangulate with alternative outcomes (gross fixed capital formation, number of firms); drop countries with data revisions; Winsorize extreme growth rates.

------------------------------------------------------------------
5. R Code Outline
------------------------------------------------------------------
```r
# Load packages
library(data.table)   # fast data wrangling
library(fixest)       # efficient high-dim panel regressions
library(ivreg)        # for IV robustness
library(bacondecomp)  # DiD decomposition diagnostic

# 1. Data loading ----------------------------------------------------------
# Assume four CSVs: industry_country_year.csv, ext_fin.csv, fin_dev.csv, controls.csv
ind_cty  <- fread("industry_country_year.csv")   # VA, GFCF, Firms, etc.
ext_fin  <- fread("external_dependence.csv")     # ExternalDependence_i
fin_dev  <- fread("financial_development.csv")   # FinDev_ct
controls <- fread("macro_controls.csv")          # Macro vars

# Merge
dat <- merge(ind_cty, ext_fin, by = "industry_code")
dat <- merge(dat, fin_dev,  by = c("country","year"))
dat <- merge(dat, controls, by = c("country","year"))

# 2. Variable construction -------------------------------------------------
dat[, Post := (year >= 1985)]
# Interaction term
dat[, treat_intensity := ExternalDependence * FinDev * Post]

# Within-decade growth (value added)
setorder(dat, country, industry_code, year)
dat[, VA_lag := shift(ValueAdded, 1), by = .(country, industry_code)]
dat[, VA_growth := log(ValueAdded) - log(VA_lag)]

# 3. Main specification ----------------------------------------------------
# DDD with country-year and industry-year FE
est_main <- feols(VA_growth ~ ExternalDependence*FinDev*Post +
                    macro_var1 + macro_var2 |
                    country^year + industry_code^year,
                  data = dat, cluster = ~country + industry_code)

summary(est_main)

# 4. IV robustness: instrument FinDev with LegalOrigin ---------------------
# First stage: FinDev on LegalOrigin plus controls
dat[, legal_english := (legal_origin == "English")]
fs <- feols(FinDev ~ legal_english + macro_var1 |
            country + year, data = dat)
summary(fs)

# Second stage
est_iv <- ivreg(VA_growth ~ ExternalDependence*FinDev*Post + macro_var1 |
                 ExternalDependence*legal_english*Post + macro_var1,
               data = dat)
summary(est_iv)

# 5. Pre-trend check (1970-1979) ------------------------------------------
pre_dat <- dat[year < 1980]
pre_est <- feols(VA_growth ~ ExternalDependence*FinDev |
                 country^year + industry_code^year,
                 data = pre_dat, cluster = ~country + industry_code)
summary(pre_est)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------
6. Expected Results
------------------------------------------------------------------
Economic theory (and corporate-finance evidence) predicts a positive effect: industries with higher external-finance dependence should grow faster by roughly 0.5–1 percentage point per year in value-added growth when moving from the 25th to 75th percentile of financial development. Therefore, the coefficient on ExternalDependence × FinDev × Post should be positive and economically meaningful (e.g., 0.6 log-points over the decade).

------------------------------------------------------------------
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (Differences-in-Differences)
------------------------------------------------------------------
C1: Parallel pre-trends documented……………………………………. 1  
C2: No anticipation (treatment not foreseen)……………………… 1  
C3: Stable units / no spillovers……………………………………….. 0.5 (some cross-border finance possible)  
C4: Exogenous treatment timing & intensity……………………… 0.5  
C5: Correct inference (two-way clustering, robust SEs)……… 1  

Total ≈ 4/5 ⇒ design is reasonably credible given mitigations above.
